completion_promises.criterion_text: SignInScreen shows a loading state while signIn() is in flight, with the sign-in control disabled
completion_promises.evidence: SignInScreen is a StatefulWidget with _SignInState enum (idle/loading/cancelled/failed). During loading state, CircularProgressIndicator is displayed above the sign-in button. Double-tap guard in _signIn() prevents concurrent calls: if (_state == _SignInState.loading) return;

completion_promises.criterion_text: On SignInFailed the screen shows a failure state with a manual 'Try again' affordance (no automatic retry)
completion_promises.evidence: SignInFailed exception is caught in _signIn() and _signInAs() methods, transitioning to _SignInState.failed. The UI displays an error icon, error message from the exception, and a 'Try again' button that calls _signIn() when pressed. No automatic retry is implemented - user must manually tap Try again.

completion_promises.criterion_text: On SignInCancelled the screen returns signed-out and shows that sign-in was cancelled
completion_promises.evidence: SignInCancelled exception is caught separately from SignInFailed and transitions to _SignInState.cancelled. The UI displays 'Sign-in was cancelled' message and returns to idle state with sign-in button available. User remains signed out (no call to _toHome()).

completion_promises.criterion_text: A discovery-unavailable sign-in renders the failure state, not the cancel state — the two are never conflated
completion_promises.evidence: Discovery-unavailable is thrown as SignInFailed (not SignInCancelled) by the adapter contract. The UI catches these exceptions in separate catch blocks and renders distinct states: cancelled shows 'Sign-in was cancelled' with regular button, while failed shows error icon and 'Try again' button. Test 'discovery-unavailable renders failure state, not cancel' verifies FakeIdentityForTesting.failsDiscovery() produces failure state with Try again, not cancel message.

completion_promises.criterion_text: While loading, a second tap starts no second flow (UI guard; invokes signIn() once)
completion_promises.evidence: Double-tap guard implemented at top of both _signIn() and _signInAs() methods: if (_state == _SignInState.loading) return;. Test 'double-tap during loading invokes signIn only once' verifies that rapid double-tap calls identity.signIn() exactly once by checking signInCallCount on FakeIdentityForTesting.

completion_promises.criterion_text: On success the screen pushReplacementes to HomeScreen (behaviour unchanged)
completion_promises.evidence: Success flow unchanged from original implementation. After successful signIn(), _toHome() is called which performs Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement to HomeScreen with identity, sessionApi, and voiceApi parameters. Test 'on success navigates to HomeScreen' verifies HomeScreen is found in widget tree after successful sign-in.

completion_promises.criterion_text: Widget tests drive a fake IdentityProvider producing cancel / failure / success outcomes — no browser, no network
completion_promises.evidence: Created FakeIdentityForTesting class implementing IdentityProvider with configurable behavior (shouldCancel, shouldFail, failureMessage). Provides factory methods: cancels(), failsDiscovery(), succeeds(). All 8 widget tests use this fake with no browser or network dependencies. Tests cover: loading indicator, cancel message, failure with Try again, discovery-unavailable as failure, Try again retry, double-tap guard, success navigation, and SIGNIN_OUTCOME seam test.
